answer:
Use rhoCentralFoam for the simulation.
Set application to rhoCentralFoam in system/controlDict.
Use a 2D rectangular domain 10 m long in x and 4 m tall in y, extruded one cell in z, with frontAndBack patches set to empty.
Center the domain on y = 0.
Define a 0.5 m tall inlet patch on the left boundary, centered at y = 0.
Define solid wall patches on the remaining left boundary above and below the inlet patch.
Define the right, top, and bottom boundaries as far-field outlet patches.
Set the inlet patch to fixedValue for U, p, and T with U = (686 0 0) m/s, p = 101325 Pa, and T = 300 K.
Set the far-field outlet patches to waveTransmissive for p and T and zeroGradient for U.
Set the solid wall patches to noSlip for U and zeroGradient for p and T.
Initialize the internal field with quiescent air at p = 101325 Pa, T = 300 K, and U = (0 0 0) m/s.
In constant/thermophysicalProperties, set thermoType to hePsiThermo with pureMixture, sutherland transport, hConstThermo thermodynamics, perfectGas equationOfState, and sensibleInternalEnergy energy.
Use standard air properties in the specie and thermodynamics dictionaries, including Cp = 1004.5 J/kg/K and molecular weight 28.96 kg/kmol.
Use the standard air Sutherland transport coefficients in the transport dictionary, for example As = 1.672e-6 and Ts = 170.672.
Set boundary conditions for any rho field as calculated from the perfect gas law using p and T.
Run with a maximum Courant number of 0.5.
Set the endTime to 0.05 s so the Mach 2 jet has time to travel through the 10 m domain at the inlet velocity of 686 m/s.
Use the rhoCentralFoam default Kurganov flux scheme in fvSolution.
